<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"eb941fe79eca57dd95366ae86963c2a1cdf1c55325b4f7e190b3aa2e662c0e20"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report is filed for aternos.com, but that host serves only a 220-byte empty frameset (its only child frame is about:⁠blank) on every path — index, 302-catch-all and ad-slot scans show no content — while the reporter's screenshots show aternos.org, which this session may not open. With no reachable page and no captured detector request, no rule can be written or validated; the report needs maintainer review rather than a fabricated selector.

## Missing information

- Reported host aternos.com serves an empty placeholder frameset; the real site (aternos.org) is off-origin and cannot be loaded: The issue's trusted URL is http:⁠//aternos.com/. In the locked adguard_cli session the reported origin returns a 220-byte frameset placeholder with an empty frame for /, and every path (/en/, /servers/) 302s to /index.html, which is the same placeholder:⁠ no visible text, no ad slots (inspect_ad_slots candidateCount 0), no third-party requests beyond local.adguard.org. The reporter's own screenshots show aternos.org, and the repository already keeps an anti-adblock rule family for aternos.org in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt, but open_page refuses any navigation to a different origin ("URL must remain on configured issue origin 'http:⁠//aternos.com'"), including https:⁠//aternos.com/. Nothing in the run instruction or guidance says how to validate a report whose reported host no longer serves the site whose symptom the reporter documented. Live evidence for the reported ads and anti-adblock wall therefore cannot be collected in any session this environment allows.

## Artifacts

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"c97db472f303d79a204f7313afbfd03eb0264d42aa8f18f69ede719a31dbe1f4"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On news.jtbc.co.kr the reporter's blank page does not reproduce (the article renders; their own AdGuard-off screenshot is blank too), but filtering does suppress the article's video:⁠ the unfiltered phase plays it while the baseline replaces it with the site's Korean anti-adblock notice. Single-rule exceptions for the IMA ad SDK and for the site's CAST beacon were applied and left the gate in place, and the remaining candidate could not be judged before the attempt budget ran out, so this is analysis-only with one unverified candidate.

## Candidate for review

`@@||mixer.mobon.net/prebid/$domain=news.jtbc.co.kr`

BaseFilter/sections/allowlist.txt

Not verified: apply_rule refused this candidate with errorKind baseline_symptom_absent before any phase judged it (the identical symptomDescription had been judged in the two earlier experiments on the same page), and remainingCandidateAttempts is 0, so it was never verified. Background for the reviewer:⁠ the video gate in div#⁠vod-container-ND10779175 ⁠> .jtbcplayer-container is filtering-caused (phase A unfiltered plays the video, baseline shows '영상 시청 안내 / …광고 차단 기능으로 인해 동영상 재생이 차단되었습니다'), but two other single-rule exceptions each applied and left the gate — @⁠@⁠||imasdk.googleapis.com/js/sdkloader/ima3.js$domain=news.jtbc.co.kr (culprit rule ||imasdk.googleapis.com^, AdGuard Base) and @⁠@⁠||cast-imp.jtbc.co.kr/trac?event=$domain=news.jtbc.co.kr (Tracking Protection beacon). This Mobon exception is a hypothesis on the page's remaining blocked ad-library request, not a confirmed fix.

## Missing information

- search_rules urlPattern cannot locate network rule families that exist: Every urlPattern query returned totalMatches 0, including patterns for rules the report itself proves exist, e.g. urlPattern "reople.co.kr", "||reople.co.kr^", "imasdk", "imasdk.googleapis.com", "sdkloader", "EmbedSDK". Only the fuzzy `domain` query returned matches (218 for jtbc.co.kr, all of them unrelated *.co.kr news sites; 952 for imasdk.googleapis.com). The run therefore could not find the repository rule family or list file that holds the culprit block (`||imasdk.googleapis.com^`, reported by get_applied_rules as AdGuard Base filter id 2) nor any existing exception family to extend, so placement had to be inferred from other BaseFilter allowlist entries instead of from the matching rule.
- Reporter list parity and apply_rule refusal inconsistency: Two reporter lists have no official baseline in this run (filterBaseline.skippedSources:⁠ third_party_catalog 'Online Malicious URL Blocklist', unresolved_name 'filterslist-KO Classic filter list'), so the reporter's exact configuration could not be reproduced by the locked AdGuard CLI baseline. Separately, the third apply_rule call was refused with errorKind baseline_symptom_absent for the same symptomDescription and the same page that the first two experiments judged (phase A unfiltered player working, phase B baseline showing the Korean ad-block gate), so that refusal appears inconsistent with the earlier accepted attempts; it consumed the remaining candidate attempt and left the third candidate unjudged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — thepostmillennial.com renders a server-side floating video ad (`aside[data-ad-placement="floating-video"]`, "ADVERTISEMENT / sponsored by Sound.Money") fixed in the bottom-right corner; it is still visible with the reporter's lists and with default filters, and hiding it was verified to remove the overlay with the page left intact. ## Rule `thepostmillennial.com##aside[data-ad-placement="floating-video"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction policy:⁠ 'The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' Not applicable — the placement is marked by the site itself as an advertisement (aria-label="Advertisement", data-tpm-ad) and carries an external advertiser (Sound.Money, links to sound.money/libby), i.e. an ordinary paid ad, not house self-promotion of the publisher's own product. Run instruction policy:⁠ paywalls and German anti-adblock walls — not applicable; the page showed no paywall, no anti-adblock message and no gating overlay, and the article content was readable. Run instruction policy for other anti-adblock walls — not applicable; no detector script appears in the captured requests (artifact:⁠har:⁠3635c858-9428-4b83-be84-1ef54f210711) and the experiment reported antiAdblockDetected false. Run instruction 'Not anti-adblock at all' clause — not triggered:⁠ no scam, phishing, malware or fake tech-support content was observed. Filter-policy document (AdguardTeam/KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md, cited by lookup_rule_guidance):⁠ third-party advertising on sites is in scope, JavaScript rules only when blocking is impossible without them — a plain element-hiding rule suffices here. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/984aacab925fc9f3dfdb2058c897d5b9dfcf3514/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 12334](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/984aacab925fc9f3dfdb2058c897d5b9dfcf3514/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L12334). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On www⁠.ilgiorno.it the reporter's blank ad areas are four empty ad shells (two 328x600 sidebar ad wrappers, the 1920x250 top ad container and a 1130x48 lower ad band) whose inner Google ad slots the Base filter already hides, leaving 1,498px of reserved blank space; a domain-scoped element-hiding rule for those shells verified in the extension (symptom resolved, layout intact), but the terminal required it scoped to ilgiorno.it alone and the run's candidate-attempt limit then refused the scoped re-validation, so the rule is carried for human review.

## Candidate for review

`ilgiorno.it##div[class^="ArticleV3_aside__ad"], #hpTopAdContainer, div[class^="ads_masthead-container__"]`

BaseFilter/sections/foreign.txt

Not verified: The exact selector list was verified in the prepared AdGuard extension session (apply_rule:⁠ environmentExperiment `verified`, visualReview `verified`, symptom `resolved`, adLayoutResidue `absent`, remainingInstances empty, pageIntegrity `intact`, observedDamage empty; all four matched ad shells measured 0x0 after filtering and the nav-to-breadcrumb gap fell from 251px to 1px, article and 'Leggi anche' module intact). That verified run carried the three-domain form `ilrestodelcarlino.it,lanazione.it,ilgiorno.it##…`; the terminal then required the candidate scoped to ilgiorno.it alone (`candidate_scope_invalid`), and apply_rule refused to re-validate the scoped form with `candidate_limit_reached` (0 of 3 attempts left). Only the domain list differs from the verified run, but the scoped rule text has no bound validation artifact, and the two sibling URLs the report names are unverified because the session is locked to the issue origin.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.wjcl.com the reporter's filters leave six empty ad sections (301/390px tall) that show only an "Advertisement" label; the rule wjcl.com#⁠#⁠.css-130fuea:⁠has(.ad-container) hides them, verified in the prepared current Chromium extension session with the page intact (the one remaining blank column is the page's own grid track, proven by DOM checks). ## Rule `wjcl.com##.css-130fuea:has(.ad-container)` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction closes only first-party advertising, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls; none applies:⁠ the report is about empty ad containers left behind after ad blocking on a Hearst Television news site, and the ads themselves are third-party-network served (securepubads.g.doubleclick.net, htlbid.com, prebid/magnite). Not anti-adblock:⁠ the prepared page showed no detector or ad-recovery overlay (antiAdblockDetected false), so the anti-adblock gate does not apply. Live evidence reproduced the reporter's defect in the prepared current extension session, so rule generation is open. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c4dc6b5b1802d68aa3c5b49b493ac63c2ff55526/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 22547](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c4dc6b5b1802d68aa3c5b49b493ac63c2ff55526/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L22547). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

### Comment
> False positive: just-design.co is blocked by AdGuard DNS (security filter: malware / phishing).
> 
> The domain belongs to a small print & graphic design business in Egypt. The site was compromised in the past (SEO spam injection with casino links), which is likely why it was listed.
> 
> It has since been fully cleaned: all old files and the old database were deleted, WordPress was reinstalled from scratch, and HTTPS redirect is enforced. The site now contains only the company's own pages (services, portfolio, quote form, contact).

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On materiels-electriques.fr the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter leaves the PrestaShop "cookiesplus" consent modal and its full-screen dark overlay covering the article; the domain-scoped element-hiding rule materiels-electriques.fr#⁠#⁠#⁠cookiesplus-overlay, #⁠cookiesplus-modal-container removed both and was verified with no page-integrity damage. ## Rule `materiels-electriques.fr###cookiesplus-overlay, #cookiesplus-modal-container` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is an in-page cookie-consent annoyance on a French site; the run instruction's close rules (first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, unnamed anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script) do not apply. It is not a paywall or anti-adblock wall:⁠ the article content is already loaded and shown, and the defect is the consent dialog plus its overlay. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter (AdGuard policy:⁠ 'this filter blocks cookie notices on web pages') is the correct home for the rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/05ebba4b3740d0e2d2a7bc2ffc0fe74a283db73f/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I’m reaching out on behalf of BioCatch, a trusted company by many of the top banks in the world, dedicated to protecting users from fraud, scams, mules and other online threats.
The domain http://we-stats.com.cdn.cloudflare.net/ is included in your DNS filter and is blocking traffic coming into our network. Your support suggested that we should apply for a recategorization.

### Proposed solution

Your support informed us that they believe this domain is being used for collecting statistics on users, which is considered tracking. We request that you re-categorize us and remove this domain from your filters.

We would appreciate your help in two ways:
 
1. Reviewing the categorization of this domain in light of its fraud-prevention purpose, and considering its removal from the DNS filter (we're happy to file the request at AdguardFilters on GitHub as you suggested, and will do so right after sending this).
2. A short call with your filter maintainers, where we can walk through exactly what is collected and why, and answer any technical or privacy questions. We're open to documenting this publicly, or to any other transparency measures that would help.

### Additional information

BioCatch's mission aligns with the broader goal of safeguarding internet users and protecting them from financial crime. your application is blocking our service (we assume it is by your use of EasyList or similar), and impacting our ability to deliver on our anti-fraud commitments and compromises our customers’ users safety. 
 
BioCatch strictly adheres to privacy standards such as GDPR, CCPA, and other regulations, and our platform is built with privacy by design at its core. Our goal is to provide users with a secure and trustworthy experience, while ensuring compliance with global privacy requirements.
 
The domain in question carries the signals (such as how a session is interacted with: typing rhythm, touch and mouse patterns, navigation behavior, but sensitive personal data (such as name, address, natiol id, email, phone, etc.) is NOT collected) that let our service tell a genuine account holder apart from a fraudster. 
 
We understand why we-stats.com.cdn.cloudflare.net was categorized as tracking: technically, it does receive data about user interaction. We'd like to explain the purpose, because we believe it differs fundamentally from the advertising and profiling traffic that AdGuard's filters are designed to stop.
 
This data is used solely for fraud detection and user protection. It is not used for advertising, marketing, cross-site profiling or resale. Without this behavioral signal, the protection that banks offer their customers would significantly weaken, and the users who are affected are the ones most likely to be targeted by fraudsters.
 
We also want to be clear that we see AdGuard as an ally, not an adversary. Both of our companies exist to protect people online: AdGuard shields users from intrusive tracking and malicious content, and BioCatch shields them from having their accounts and savings compromised. We share the same goal, and we'd much rather work with you than around you.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's first crossed-out module (the "Okumaya devam et" recommendation carousel) is already removed by the published ||tgrthaber.com/components/continuereading rule, and the second (a site-wide injected "günün özeti" video block) is hidden by a narrow cosmetic rule, but both tested candidates were rejected by the vision review because it also counted the news site's own headline and related carousels as the same symptom, so no safe verified rule was produced.

## Still visible after the rule

- Meteoroloji 18 ili sarı kodla uyardı / KAR SAĞANAK FIRTINA ALARMI carousel above YORUM YAZ — Horizontal unrelated weather-news recommendation carousel with left/right arrows and numbered pagination 1–20; it visually repeats the reporter's crossed-out related-content carousel of injected/unrelated content.
- Article body, large black 16:⁠9 panel below the introductory paragraph at the bottom of the viewport — Large black 16:⁠9 embedded media/video panel in the article body, matching the reported in-article video-content location. At this overview scale only the poster area is visible; no orange annotation or player controls are legible.

## Missing information

- Policy scope for a site's own injected non-ad video/self-promotion modules: The run instruction's Filter policy only covers "the site's own advertising (first-party ads)" (no rule; recommend closing) and the filter-policy document's Widgets entry excludes "Widgets for self-promotion and site-specific promotional activities", but neither states how to treat a first-party, non-advertising content module the site injects into every article (here:⁠ the tgrthaber.com body video block served from v.tgrthaber.com/gunun-ozeti/ with data-stick-after-seen). I needed a rule on whether such injected self-promotional video modules are in scope for the Widgets/Other Annoyances filters, and on how to scope a rule when the vision review also counts the site's own headline/recommendation carousels as the "same symptom family".

Open NAVER Whale. > 2. Enable AdGuard filtering. > 3. Visit: > > https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=S1N16&view_type=sm > > 4. Make sure the article list is displayed in **summary view**. > 5. Click page `2` at the bottom of the page. > 6. Observe that: > - the view changes unexpectedly to title-only mode, and/or > - the second page is not loaded correctly, > - pagination stops working normally. > > 7. Disable AdGuard filtering. > 8. Reload the same page and repeat the same steps. > 9. Pagination works normally and the selected list view is preserved. > > ## Expected behavior > > With AdGuard enabled: > > - Summary view should remain in summary view. > - Title-only view should remain in title-only view. > - Clicking page `2`, `3`, etc. should load the corresponding article list correctly. > > ## Actual behavior > > With AdGuard enabled: > > - Summary view may unexpectedly change to title-only view. > - Page 2 and later pages do not load correctly. > - The article list effectively remains stuck on page 1. > - Pagination works normally again after AdGuard is disabled. > > ## Additional information > > This appears to be a filtering-related site breakage rather than an issue with the website itself, because the same pagination works correctly when AdGuard is turned off. > > It may be worth checking whether one of the AdGuard filtering rules is blocking a request, script, or parameter used by: > > - pagination > - article list view switching > - page number handling > > ## Screenshots > > - Screenshots 1–2: AdGuard enabled — pagination/list view broken > - Screenshots 3–4: AdGuard disabled — pagination works normally > > Please check for a possible false positive or site compatibility issue in the filtering rules. ### Screenshots

issue.title: facebook.com: sponsored-post #%# MutationObserver rules in Base filter cause severe main-thread jank (~10 s per page load)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue (Base filter 2.5.2.64, updated 2026-11-06)
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date
- [x] Disabling the JS rules on the site resolves the issue

### What product do you use?
AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version
5.5.3.49 (MV3)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website or app doesn't work properly (severe slowness / freezing)

### Which browser(s) do you use?
Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Which device do you use?
Desktop (Windows 11, Intel i7-1185G7, 32 GB RAM, the machine itself is idle)

### Where is the problem encountered?
https://www.facebook.com/ (feed, groups and single post pages)

### What filters do you have enabled?
- Ad Blocking: AdGuard Base filter
- Other: AdGuard Search Ads and Self-Promotion filter, EasyList Hebrew

### Issue details

Facebook is constantly slow and freezes while loading and scrolling. I profiled it with Chrome DevTools (performance trace + CPU profile) and found that almost all of the extra main-thread time comes from the facebook.com `#%#` JS rules in AdGuard Base filter that hide sponsored posts.

These rules create a `MutationObserver` on `document` with `{childList: true, subtree: true}`. On every mutation the callback runs `document.querySelectorAll()` with a very large selector list (`div[data-pagelet^="FeedUnit"]…`, `div[role="feed"] > div…`, `#ssrb_feed_start + div …`, and so on) and inspects `__reactFiber` props on the results. Facebook mutates the DOM constantly, so the callback runs hundreds of times while the page loads and keeps running during scrolling. The callback is not throttled or debounced.

**Measured on the same post page, with a MutationObserver wrapper injected before page scripts to time each observer callback:**

| | Before | After adding `@@\|\|facebook.com^$jsinject` |
|---|---|---|
| DOMContentLoaded | 15.0 s / 16.9 s (one run > 60 s) | **3.3 s / 2.4 s** |
| load event | 18.3 s / 64 s | **4.2 s / 2.7 s** |
| Time spent in AdGuard observer callbacks | **~11.4 s** | 0 |
| Time spent in all page MutationObservers | > 11.4 s | 0.13–0.25 s |

Breakdown of the observer callbacks before the fix (one page load):

| Rule (AdGuard Base filter) | Calls | Total time | Max single call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feed sponsored posts: `!function(){var b=0,d=[];new MutationObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll("div[data-pagelet^=\"FeedUnit\"]…, div[role=\"feed\"] > span…, #ssrb_feed_start + div > div[class]…` | 569 | **10,396 ms** | 100 ms |
| Sidebar (`div[role="complementary"]`, `__reactFiber`): `(()=>{const e=new MutationObserver((()=>{const n=document.querySelectorAll('div[role="complementary"] …` | 569 | 911 ms | 9 ms |
| Old interface (`div[id^='mount_']` / `hyperfeed_story_id` / `socheck`) | 569 | 119 ms | 2 ms |

In the CPU profile, `querySelectorAll` called from these callbacks accounted for ~10 s of self time out of ~26 s of main-thread activity. All other extensions together used under 0.3 s.

**Suggestions**
- Debounce or throttle the observer callback (for example, collect mutations and process them once per `requestAnimationFrame` or `requestIdleCallback`).
- Query only the added nodes (`mutation.addedNodes`) instead of re-running the full-document `querySelectorAll` on every mutation.
- Drop the selectors for the old Facebook interface (`hyperfeed_story_id`, `userContentWrapper`), which no longer exists.

**Workaround:** the user rule `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject` removes the freeze completely, at the cost of some sponsored posts coming back.

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

issue.title: facebook.com: sponsored-post #%# MutationObserver rules in Base filter cause severe main-thread jank (~10 s per page load)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue (Base filter 2.5.2.64, updated 2026-11-06)
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date
- [x] Disabling the JS rules on the site resolves the issue

### What product do you use?
AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version
5.5.3.49 (MV3)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website or app doesn't work properly (severe slowness / freezing)

### Which browser(s) do you use?
Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Which device do you use?
Desktop (Windows 11, Intel i7-1185G7, 32 GB RAM, the machine itself is idle)

### Where is the problem encountered?
https://www.facebook.com/ (feed, groups and single post pages)

### What filters do you have enabled?
- Ad Blocking: AdGuard Base filter
- Other: AdGuard Search Ads and Self-Promotion filter, EasyList Hebrew

### Issue details

Facebook is constantly slow and freezes while loading and scrolling. I profiled it with Chrome DevTools (performance trace + CPU profile) and found that almost all of the extra main-thread time comes from the facebook.com `#%#` JS rules in AdGuard Base filter that hide sponsored posts.

These rules create a `MutationObserver` on `document` with `{childList: true, subtree: true}`. On every mutation the callback runs `document.querySelectorAll()` with a very large selector list (`div[data-pagelet^="FeedUnit"]…`, `div[role="feed"] > div…`, `#ssrb_feed_start + div …`, and so on) and inspects `__reactFiber` props on the results. Facebook mutates the DOM constantly, so the callback runs hundreds of times while the page loads and keeps running during scrolling. The callback is not throttled or debounced.

**Measured on the same post page, with a MutationObserver wrapper injected before page scripts to time each observer callback:**

| | Before | After adding `@@\|\|facebook.com^$jsinject` |
|---|---|---|
| DOMContentLoaded | 15.0 s / 16.9 s (one run > 60 s) | **3.3 s / 2.4 s** |
| load event | 18.3 s / 64 s | **4.2 s / 2.7 s** |
| Time spent in AdGuard observer callbacks | **~11.4 s** | 0 |
| Time spent in all page MutationObservers | > 11.4 s | 0.13–0.25 s |

Breakdown of the observer callbacks before the fix (one page load):

| Rule (AdGuard Base filter) | Calls | Total time | Max single call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feed sponsored posts: `!function(){var b=0,d=[];new MutationObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll("div[data-pagelet^=\"FeedUnit\"]…, div[role=\"feed\"] > span…, #ssrb_feed_start + div > div[class]…` | 569 | **10,396 ms** | 100 ms |
| Sidebar (`div[role="complementary"]`, `__reactFiber`): `(()=>{const e=new MutationObserver((()=>{const n=document.querySelectorAll('div[role="complementary"] …` | 569 | 911 ms | 9 ms |
| Old interface (`div[id^='mount_']` / `hyperfeed_story_id` / `socheck`) | 569 | 119 ms | 2 ms |

In the CPU profile, `querySelectorAll` called from these callbacks accounted for ~10 s of self time out of ~26 s of main-thread activity. All other extensions together used under 0.3 s.

**Suggestions**
- Debounce or throttle the observer callback (for example, collect mutations and process them once per `requestAnimationFrame` or `requestIdleCallback`).
- Query only the added nodes (`mutation.addedNodes`) instead of re-running the full-document `querySelectorAll` on every mutation.
- Drop the selectors for the old Facebook interface (`hyperfeed_story_id`, `userContentWrapper`), which no longer exists.

**Workaround:** the user rule `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject` removes the freeze completely, at the cost of some sponsored posts coming back.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — api.debtstrike.eu shows a first-party, inline-styled privacy/cookie notice (div#⁠ds-prywatnosc) fixed to the bottom of the viewport, and no existing rule covers it. Hiding it with api.debtstrike.eu#⁠#⁠#⁠ds-prywatnosc removed the banner with the page left intact in the reporter-profile baseline. ## Rule `api.debtstrike.eu###ds-prywatnosc` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Policy check:⁠ this is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall — the page shows a privacy/cookie notice, not an ad-blocker detection message. None of the instruction's close-without-a-rule cases applies. Not an anti-adblock wall at all, so no detector-script evidence requirement applies; the element is baked into the served page and is handled as an ordinary Annoyances (Cookie Notices) rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5e7f68c61f1c4133ba3d26d3faee04901882b0b5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42596079789 Automated analysis against filters at `5e7f68c`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — legenda-dom.ru shows a fixed full-width cookie-consent bar ("Мы используем cookie…" with "Принять cookie"/"Закрыть") that no current filter hides; the domain-scoped hiding rule `legenda-dom.ru##div[class^="CookieLaw_cookieLaw__"]` was verified in the CLI filtering session — the bar disappears and the page stays intact. ## Rule `legenda-dom.ru##div[class^="CookieLaw_cookieLaw__"]` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice (annoyance), not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for exactly this class of element; its policy states that hiding the notice is sufficient in most cases, which matches the observed page-owned banner that gates no content. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5e7f68c61f1c4133ba3d26d3faee04901882b0b5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42595565291 Automated analysis against filters at `5e7f68c`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

### Comment
> Since you don’t ask the right questions I could not answer properly. However, when I use the app “SmartNews” from the Apple App Store I realize I get ads. Then I look into the Apple settings safari extensions and none are there. I deleted the app, re-installed it, the extensions where there, I turned all of them on, open smart news, and have no ads. 30 minutes later I look into the settings extension and do not have any extension whatsoever (see pic). issue.title: facebook.com: sponsored-post #%# MutationObserver rules in Base filter cause severe main-thread jank (~10 s per page load)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue (Base filter 2.5.2.64, updated 2026-11-06)
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date
- [x] Disabling the JS rules on the site resolves the issue

### What product do you use?
AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version
5.5.3.49 (MV3)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website or app doesn't work properly (severe slowness / freezing)

### Which browser(s) do you use?
Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Which device do you use?
Desktop (Windows 11, Intel i7-1185G7, 32 GB RAM, the machine itself is idle)

### Where is the problem encountered?
https://www.facebook.com/ (feed, groups and single post pages)

### What filters do you have enabled?
- Ad Blocking: AdGuard Base filter
- Other: AdGuard Search Ads and Self-Promotion filter, EasyList Hebrew

### Issue details

Facebook is constantly slow and freezes while loading and scrolling. I profiled it with Chrome DevTools (performance trace + CPU profile) and found that almost all of the extra main-thread time comes from the facebook.com `#%#` JS rules in AdGuard Base filter that hide sponsored posts.

These rules create a `MutationObserver` on `document` with `{childList: true, subtree: true}`. On every mutation the callback runs `document.querySelectorAll()` with a very large selector list (`div[data-pagelet^="FeedUnit"]…`, `div[role="feed"] > div…`, `#ssrb_feed_start + div …`, and so on) and inspects `__reactFiber` props on the results. Facebook mutates the DOM constantly, so the callback runs hundreds of times while the page loads and keeps running during scrolling. The callback is not throttled or debounced.

**Measured on the same post page, with a MutationObserver wrapper injected before page scripts to time each observer callback:**

| | Before | After adding `@@\|\|facebook.com^$jsinject` |
|---|---|---|
| DOMContentLoaded | 15.0 s / 16.9 s (one run > 60 s) | **3.3 s / 2.4 s** |
| load event | 18.3 s / 64 s | **4.2 s / 2.7 s** |
| Time spent in AdGuard observer callbacks | **~11.4 s** | 0 |
| Time spent in all page MutationObservers | > 11.4 s | 0.13–0.25 s |

Breakdown of the observer callbacks before the fix (one page load):

| Rule (AdGuard Base filter) | Calls | Total time | Max single call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feed sponsored posts: `!function(){var b=0,d=[];new MutationObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll("div[data-pagelet^=\"FeedUnit\"]…, div[role=\"feed\"] > span…, #ssrb_feed_start + div > div[class]…` | 569 | **10,396 ms** | 100 ms |
| Sidebar (`div[role="complementary"]`, `__reactFiber`): `(()=>{const e=new MutationObserver((()=>{const n=document.querySelectorAll('div[role="complementary"] …` | 569 | 911 ms | 9 ms |
| Old interface (`div[id^='mount_']` / `hyperfeed_story_id` / `socheck`) | 569 | 119 ms | 2 ms |

In the CPU profile, `querySelectorAll` called from these callbacks accounted for ~10 s of self time out of ~26 s of main-thread activity. All other extensions together used under 0.3 s.

**Suggestions**
- Debounce or throttle the observer callback (for example, collect mutations and process them once per `requestAnimationFrame` or `requestIdleCallback`).
- Query only the added nodes (`mutation.addedNodes`) instead of re-running the full-document `querySelectorAll` on every mutation.
- Drop the selectors for the old Facebook interface (`hyperfeed_story_id`, `userContentWrapper`), which no longer exists.

**Workaround:** the user rule `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject` removes the freeze completely, at the cost of some sponsored posts coming back.

comment.body: Most of these `MutationObserver` rules for Facebook seem to be obsolete now, so I just disabled them.

The problem persists. > > **Important test results:** > - With AdGuard enabled, the repeat function switches off between songs. > - With AdGuard disabled, repeat stays enabled across several songs, but YouTube advertisements appear. > - Screenshots showing both situations are attached. > > I have used AdGuard successfully for a long time, and YouTube's repeat function previously worked correctly. > > Please investigate whether an AdGuard filtering rule is interfering with YouTube's playlist repeat function. I would appreciate a solution that allows me to keep blocking advertisements while using repeat. ### Screenshots

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://ya.tv/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fya.tv%2F) ### Comment > Здравствуйте! > > У меня на Яндекс ТВ Станции в системном плеере Яндекса («Я.ТВ Веб-плеер») просматривается контент с Rutube. Наблюдаю жёсткий конфликт между блокировкой рекламы и сохранением прогресса просмотра. > > Сценарий воспроизведения (проверено многократно): > > 1. При включённой фильтрации для «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер»: реклама блокируется, но прогресс просмотра (номер серии и таймкод) не сохраняется. Плеер показывает устаревшую позицию (например, «8 серия» вместо «12»). > 2. При добавлении «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер» в исключения фильтрации: прогресс просмотра начинает сохраняться корректно, но реклама возвращается в полном объёме (не редкие проскоки, а полноценные вставки). Редкие микропроскоки длительностью менее секунды, которые наблюдались ранее, объясняются только работой DNS‑фильтрации при отключённой HTTPS‑фильтрации для приложения. > 3. Включение/отключение защиты от трекинга (антитрекинг) в настройках AdGuard не влияет на проблему. > > Предполагаемая причина: служебный запрос для синхронизации позиции просмотра блокируется вместе с рекламой, потому что он идёт через те же домены/эндпоинты. В результате фильтрация либо ломает прогресс, либо (при полном исключении приложения) оставляет рекламу нетронутой. > > Что уже пробовал: > * Отключение антитрекинг‑фильтров — без эффекта. > * Исключение приложения «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер» из фильтрации — прогресс сохраняется, реклама возвращается в полном объёме. > * Анализ поведения при включённом DNS‑фильтре и выключенном HTTPS‑фильтре для плеера — DNS‑фильтрация даёт лишь частичный эффект (редкие микропроскоки), полноценной блокировки рекламы без HTTPS‑фильтрации не получается. > > Прошу помочь: > 1. Подсказать, какой именно запрос (домен/путь/API‑эндпоинт) отвечает за синхронизацию прогресса просмотра в этом сценарии, чтобы можно было добавить точечное исключение и сохранить блокировку рекламы. > 2. Либо добавить в официальные фильтры корректное исключение, которое позволит одновременно блокировать рекламу и не ломать сохранение прогресса. ### Screenshots

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://ya.tv/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fya.tv%2F) ### Comment > Здравствуйте! > > У меня на Яндекс ТВ Станции в системном плеере Яндекса («Я.ТВ Веб-плеер») просматривается контент с Rutube. Наблюдаю жёсткий конфликт между блокировкой рекламы и сохранением прогресса просмотра. > > Сценарий воспроизведения (проверено многократно): > > 1. При включённой фильтрации для «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер»: реклама блокируется, но прогресс просмотра (номер серии и таймкод) не сохраняется. Плеер показывает устаревшую позицию (например, «8 серия» вместо «12»). > 2. При добавлении «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер» в исключения фильтрации: прогресс просмотра начинает сохраняться корректно, но реклама возвращается в полном объёме (не редкие проскоки, а полноценные вставки). Редкие микропроскоки длительностью менее секунды, которые наблюдались ранее, объясняются только работой DNS‑фильтрации при отключённой HTTPS‑фильтрации для приложения. > 3. Включение/отключение защиты от трекинга (антитрекинг) в настройках AdGuard не влияет на проблему. > > Предполагаемая причина: служебный запрос для синхронизации позиции просмотра блокируется вместе с рекламой, потому что он идёт через те же домены/эндпоинты. В результате фильтрация либо ломает прогресс, либо (при полном исключении приложения) оставляет рекламу нетронутой. > > Что уже пробовал: > * Отключение антитрекинг‑фильтров — без эффекта. > * Исключение приложения «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер» из фильтрации — прогресс сохраняется, реклама возвращается в полном объёме. > * Анализ поведения при включённом DNS‑фильтре и выключенном HTTPS‑фильтре для плеера — DNS‑фильтрация даёт лишь частичный эффект (редкие микропроскоки), полноценной блокировки рекламы без HTTPS‑фильтрации не получается. > > Прошу помочь: > 1. Подсказать, какой именно запрос (домен/путь/API‑эндпоинт) отвечает за синхронизацию прогресса просмотра в этом сценарии, чтобы можно было добавить точечное исключение и сохранить блокировку рекламы. > 2. Либо добавить в официальные фильтры корректное исключение, которое позволит одновременно блокировать рекламу и не ломать сохранение прогресса. ### Screenshots

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=S1N16&view_type=sm](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.einfomax.co.kr%2Fnews%2FarticleList.html%3Fsc_section_code%3DS1N16%26view_type%3Dsm) ### Comment > ## Title > > Pagination and list view break on `news.einfomax.co.kr` when AdGuard filtering is enabled > > ## Website > > https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=S1N16&view_type=sm > > Section: Bonds / FX (`채권/외환`) > > ## Environment > > - OS: Windows 11 > - Browser: NAVER Whale > - Ad blocker: AdGuard > - AdGuard filtering: Enabled > - AdGuard version: [please insert version] > > ## Problem > > When AdGuard filtering is enabled, pagination on the article list page of `news.einfomax.co.kr` does not work correctly. > > The issue is especially reproducible in the **summary view**. > > When I open the Bonds / FX article list in summary view and click page `2`: > > 1. The list unexpectedly changes from **summary view** to **title-only view**. > 2. The website does not load the actual second page correctly. > 3. It effectively returns to or remains on the first-page article list. > 4. Further pagination also fails, so I cannot browse page 2, 3, etc. normally. > > The same problem also occurs when using the site's **title-only article list**: with AdGuard enabled, only the first page can be viewed correctly and navigation to later pages does not work. > > ## Steps to reproduce > > 1. Open NAVER Whale. > 2. Enable AdGuard filtering. > 3. Visit: > > https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=S1N16&view_type=sm > > 4. Make sure the article list is displayed in **summary view**. > 5. Click page `2` at the bottom of the page. > 6. Observe that: > - the view changes unexpectedly to title-only mode, and/or > - the second page is not loaded correctly, > - pagination stops working normally. > > 7. Disable AdGuard filtering. > 8. Reload the same page and repeat the same steps. > 9. Pagination works normally and the selected list view is preserved. > > ## Expected behavior > > With AdGuard enabled: > > - Summary view should remain in summary view. > - Title-only view should remain in title-only view. > - Clicking page `2`, `3`, etc. should load the corresponding article list correctly. > > ## Actual behavior > > With AdGuard enabled: > > - Summary view may unexpectedly change to title-only view. > - Page 2 and later pages do not load correctly. > - The article list effectively remains stuck on page 1. > - Pagination works normally again after AdGuard is disabled. > > ## Additional information > > This appears to be a filtering-related site breakage rather than an issue with the website itself, because the same pagination works correctly when AdGuard is turned off. > > It may be worth checking whether one of the AdGuard filtering rules is blocking a request, script, or parameter used by: > > - pagination > - article list view switching > - page number handling > > ## Screenshots > > - Screenshots 1–2: AdGuard enabled — pagination/list view broken > - Screenshots 3–4: AdGuard disabled — pagination works normally > > Please check for a possible false positive or site compatibility issue in the filtering rules. ### Screenshots

### Prerequisites - [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml); - [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue; - [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date; - [x] Browser version is up-to-date; - [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue. ### What product do you use? AdGuard for Windows ### AdGuard version 8.0.3 ### What type of problem have you encountered? Missed ads or ad leftovers ### Which browser(s) do you use? Microsoft Edge ### Which device do you use? Desktop ### Where is the problem encountered? https://es.wlygrowth.com/todesk.html ### Ad Blocking AdGuard Base filter ### Privacy AdGuard URL Tracking filter, EasyPrivacy, AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, Legitimate URL Shortener ### Social Widgets _No response_ ### Annoyances Adblock Warning Removal List ### Security uBlock Origin – Badware risks, Scam Blocklist by DurableNapkin, Phishing URL Blocklist, Online Malicious URL Blocklist ### Other _No response_ ### DNS filters AdGuard DNS filter ### Language-specific AdGuard Chinese filter, CJX's Annoyances List, xinggsf ### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled? _No response_ ### Add your comment and screenshots 1. This domain (`wlygrowth.com`) is a deceptive distribution network for Adware/PUP. It hosts fake landing pages (e.g., `/todesk.html`) to hijack user downloads. **Why this should be blocked:** 1. **Identical Malicious Payload:** Different pages (ToDesk, NetEase Music) download the exact same file (`MD5: 39EF6D1077112557F27EA07AFA407626`). 2. **Security Threat:** Kaspersky flags the payload as `HEUR:AdWare.Win32.Ludi.gen`. 3. **Spoofed Signature:** The installer's UAC prompt shows "Chengdu Qilu Technology" (Ludashi), not the official software publishers. 4. **Silent Tracking:** The PUP silently connects to `api.ludashisafe.com`, which **AdGuard Security filter already blocks**. 5. **Evasion:** The forced installation of "Jifeng Software Market" hides from the Start Menu to prevent uninstallation. I suggest blocking the entire domain to stop this deceptive network: `||wlygrowth.com^` 2. Screenshots
Screenshot 1:Kaspersky flags the downloaded file (regardless of the name) as `HEUR:AdWare.Win32.Ludi.gen`.
Screenshot 2:The UAC prompt shows the publisher is "成都奇鲁科技有限公司" (Ludashi), not the official software publishers (ToDesk or NetEase).
Screenshot 3:The execution forces the installation of "Jifeng Software Market".
Screenshot 4:AdGuard blocks silent connections to `api.ludashisafe.com` and `update.ludashisafe.com` during the process.
Screenshot 5:The installed market does not appear in the Start Menu, only in the Apps list. No desktop shortcut is created.
Screenshot 6:Another Adware From `https://es.wlygrowth.com/Music163.html`.ESET flags the downloaded file (regardless of the name) as `Win32/Qihoo360.K Potentially Unwanted Ap`, according to VirusTotal.
Screenshot 7:The UAC prompt shows the publisher is "Beijing Qihu Technology Co., Ltd" (Qihoo360), not the official NetEase software publishers "NetEase (Hangzhou) Network Co., Ltd".
Screenshot 8:The execution forces the installation of "360 Security Guard", which is an anti-virus software.
Screenshot 9:The installed anti-virus software does not appear in the Start Menu, only in the Apps list. No desktop shortcut is created.
### Privacy - [x] I agree to follow this condition

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"4013e60dc960da7c93bf07e419385807e89e5e5b92177f2ff896c569d8a97cb5"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reporter's arrows point only at speedof.me's own certificate self-promotion (two fixed edge cards, a promo popup and an upsell line), which is the site's own advertising. The run instruction's filter policy forbids a rule for first-party ads, so the report is recommended for closing, with a note that the repository's self-promo section still carries out-of-date speedof.me selectors for a maintainer to judge.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy, verbatim:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter-annotated content is speedof.me's own advertising for its own paid certificate product. Live evidence shows the annotated content is first-party self-promotion, not a third-party ad placement:⁠ the two fixed side cards are rendered by speedof.me's own markup (obfuscated classes cimsd-ss / ala-vj, fixed position, no external request behind them) and promote the site's own certificate service; the reporter's screenshot arrows point at these same cards plus a certificate promo popup and the 'Applying for a remote job?' upsell line. No third-party advertising defect is present to fix:⁠ the page's only ad-network requests (pagead2.googlesyndication.com, fundingchoicesmessages.google.com) are already blocked by rules in the loaded baseline, and the page's ad slots (.intro-ad-footer, .api-ad-footer) are already hidden by existing Base filter rules speedof.me#⁠#⁠.intro-ad-footer and speedof.me#⁠#⁠.api-ad-footer. Recorded tension for the maintainer, not resolved by the agent:⁠ AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt already carries speedof.me self-promo rules (.home-promos, .hero-promos, body ⁠> [⁠class]⁠:⁠has(⁠> a[⁠href="/api?src=rail"]⁠)), and the Other Annoyances filter's stated purpose includes blocking website self-promotion considered annoying; those legacy selectors no longer match the redesigned markup. If maintainers prefer the self-promo-annoyance route over the run instruction's first-party-ads rule, the report is theirs to handle.

## Artifacts

issue.title: [Missed Adware/PUP] wlygrowth.com distributes deceptive fake installers (ToDesk, NetEase)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites - [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml); - [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue; - [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date; - [x] Browser version is up-to-date; - [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue. ### What product do you use? AdGuard for Windows ### AdGuard version 8.0.3 ### What type of problem have you encountered? Missed ads or ad leftovers ### Which browser(s) do you use? Microsoft Edge ### Which device do you use? Desktop ### Where is the problem encountered? https://es.wlygrowth.com/todesk.html ### Ad Blocking AdGuard Base filter ### Privacy AdGuard URL Tracking filter, EasyPrivacy, AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, Legitimate URL Shortener ### Social Widgets _No response_ ### Annoyances Adblock Warning Removal List ### Security uBlock Origin – Badware risks, Scam Blocklist by DurableNapkin, Phishing URL Blocklist, Online Malicious URL Blocklist ### Other _No response_ ### DNS filters AdGuard DNS filter ### Language-specific AdGuard Chinese filter, CJX's Annoyances List, xinggsf ### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled? _No response_ ### Add your comment and screenshots 1. This domain (`wlygrowth.com`) is a deceptive distribution network for Adware/PUP. It hosts fake landing pages (e.g., `/todesk.html`) to hijack user downloads. **Why this should be blocked:** 1. **Identical Malicious Payload:** Different pages (ToDesk, NetEase Music) download the exact same file (`MD5: 39EF6D1077112557F27EA07AFA407626`). 2. **Security Threat:** Kaspersky flags the payload as `HEUR:AdWare.Win32.Ludi.gen`. 3. **Spoofed Signature:** The installer's UAC prompt shows "Chengdu Qilu Technology" (Ludashi), not the official software publishers. 4. **Silent Tracking:** The PUP silently connects to `api.ludashisafe.com`, which **AdGuard Security filter already blocks**. 5. **Evasion:** The forced installation of "Jifeng Software Market" hides from the Start Menu to prevent uninstallation. I suggest blocking the entire domain to stop this deceptive network: `||wlygrowth.com^` 2. Screenshots
Screenshot 1:Kaspersky flags the downloaded file (regardless of the name) as `HEUR:AdWare.Win32.Ludi.gen`.
Screenshot 2:The UAC prompt shows the publisher is "成都奇鲁科技有限公司" (Ludashi), not the official software publishers (ToDesk or NetEase).
Screenshot 3:The execution forces the installation of "Jifeng Software Market".
Screenshot 4:AdGuard blocks silent connections to `api.ludashisafe.com` and `update.ludashisafe.com` during the process.
Screenshot 5:The installed market does not appear in the Start Menu, only in the Apps list. No desktop shortcut is created.
Screenshot 6:Another Adware From `https://es.wlygrowth.com/Music163.html`.ESET flags the downloaded file (regardless of the name) as `Win32/Qihoo360.K Potentially Unwanted Ap`, according to VirusTotal.
Screenshot 7:The UAC prompt shows the publisher is "Beijing Qihu Technology Co., Ltd" (Qihoo360), not the official NetEase software publishers "NetEase (Hangzhou) Network Co., Ltd".
Screenshot 8:The execution forces the installation of "360 Security Guard", which is an anti-virus software.
Screenshot 9:The installed anti-virus software does not appear in the Start Menu, only in the Apps list. No desktop shortcut is created.
### Privacy - [x] I agree to follow this condition

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — one-piecewiki.com shows a self-hosted "Your privacy choices" cookie modal that also applies html.wc-consent-open{overflow:⁠hidden}, locking page scrolling; recording the "Essential only" choice before the site's inline consent script runs removes the banner and the lock, and that scriptlet rule passed the before/after browser experiment. ## Rule `one-piecewiki.com#%#//scriptlet('set-local-storage-item', 'wc_consent', 'denied')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a cookie/consent banner (annoyance), not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall; none of the run instruction's close-without-rule categories applies. The page shows no anti-adblock message:⁠ the overlay is the site's own 'Your privacy choices' consent dialog for analytics/advertising cookies, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle. No rule exists for one-piecewiki.com in any repository filter, and the reporter's own enabled lists apply no cookie-notice rule to the site, so rule generation is appropriate. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/10665b9d01c2c84fa3ba3d193cc732dc5ad1f417/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://tierramilenaria.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftierramilenaria.com%2F)

### Comment
> False positive: tierramilenaria.com is blocked by AdGuard DNS (default server returns 94.140.14.33), but it is a legitimate website.
> 
> tierramilenaria.com is the official site of Tierra Milenaria Tours, a travel agency in Arequipa, Peru. It has no malware, phishing, ads or third-party trackers. Google Safe Browsing reports no unsafe content, and Quad9's tester shows the listing comes from a ThreatConnect feed. The site was hit by spam bots against its contact forms in Sep-Oct 2026 (all blocked by the site); the site itself never hosted anything malicious.
> 
> Steps to reproduce:
> 1. Use AdGuard DNS default (94.140.14.14).
> 2. Open https://tierramilenaria.com/
> 3. The domain resolves to 94.140.14.33 (blocked) and the browser cannot open the site. With the non-filtering server (94.140.14.140) it resolves to the Hostinger CDN and loads normally.
> 
> Our international customers cannot reach the website because of this block. Please unblock tierramilenaria.com and www.tierramilenaria.com. Thank you.

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.youtube.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2F) ### Comment > **Problem: YouTube playlist repeat switches off when AdGuard is enabled.** > > For approximately four months, YouTube's playlist repeat function has stopped working correctly in Google Chrome. > > When I enable repeat, it switches off when the next video starts. This happens across multiple playlists and on three different computers. > > I have updated AdGuard's filters, refreshed YouTube, and tested with another ad-blocking extension disabled. <!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"ed4a4e6ecdbc95f5d398117b5b6a1b5c81cd6726d05e9281a267cf8c84ac950c"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

wispbyte.com's anti-adblock wall lives in the login-gated client area:⁠ the reported URL returned HTTP 200 but only the site's login page, and public pages show no wall, so no detector script appears in the captured requests. Per the run instruction's anti-adblock policy, this report is handed to a maintainer instead of a rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction policy, anti-adblock clause:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer.' The captured requests for the reported URL contain no detector script, so no rule may be generated and the report goes to a maintainer. The wall is not a German site's wall:⁠ the modal from the reporter screenshot is English ('Your ad blocker ate our ads', 'Check again'), so the German anti-adblock clause that recommends closing does not apply. The reported page sits behind authentication, so the detector could not be captured in this run:⁠ a maintainer with an authenticated session can capture the loader behind the wall and finish the fix.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42635080070
